name: Nandi Hills
shortDescription: Iconic sunrise viewpoint with historic hill fort
description: Nandi Hills (Nandi Durga) is a historic hill fortress in Chikkaballapur district at 1,478 m elevation. Once the summer retreat of Tipu Sultan, it features fort ruins, Tipu's Drop cliff, and the ancient Bhoga Nandeeshwara Temple at the foothills. Accessible by road; popular for sunrise views.

name: Skandagiri
shortDescription: Popular night trek to hill fort with sunrise cloud inversion views
description: Skandagiri (Kalavara Durga) is a moderate night trek to a historic 18th-century hill fort at 1,350 m elevation. The 8 km round-trip trail (4 km ascent + 4 km descent) traverses forest and rocky ridgelines to summit ruins with panoramic views. Mandatory permit required via Karnataka Forest Department.
permitDetails: Mandatory online permit via Karnataka Eco-Tourism portal. Capped at ~150–200 permits/day. Book at aranyavihaara.karnataka.gov.in. No walk-ins.
parkingDetails: Parking at base village Kalavara (₹50–100 per vehicle)
waterDetails: No water sources on trail. Carry at least 2L water per person.

sourceReferences.title: Karnataka Forest Department - Aranya Vihaara Booking Portal

name: Chunchi Falls
shortDescription: Scenic waterfall on Arkavathi River near Kanakapura
description: Chunchi Falls is a waterfall on the Arkavathi River in Ramanagara district, best visited during monsoon season when water flow is high. Located ~20 km from Kanakapura. Limited official information available on facilities, timings, or fees.

name: Savandurga Hill
shortDescription: Asia's largest monolith hill with trekking routes
description: Savandurga (Savana Durga) is a massive monolith hill at 1,226 m elevation in Ramanagara district, near Magadi. It is described as the largest monolith in Asia and offers trekking routes. A medicinal herb garden is located at the foothill. Limited official information on specific timings, fees, or permit requirements.

name: Makalidurga
shortDescription: Moderate hill fort trek with railway tunnel views
description: Makalidurga is a hill fort at 1,117 m elevation in Bengaluru Rural district, near Doddaballapur. The moderate 4 km one-way trail (8 km round trip) leads to fort ruins and a Shiva temple at the summit, with views of Gundamagere Lake and the railway line below. Mandatory permit required via Karnataka Forest Department.
permitDetails: Online forest department booking required via Karnataka Eco-Tourism portal. Slots 6:00 AM–10:00 AM.
parkingDetails: Parking available at base near Makalidurga Railway Station
waterDetails: No water on trail. Carry water from base.

name: Anthargange
shortDescription: Volcanic rock formations, caves, and spring-fed temples
description: Anthargange (Antara Gange) is a hill area 3 km west of Kolar city, known for volcanic rock formations, natural caves, and a perennial spring emerging from a Basavanna (Nandi) sculpture. Features 250 steps to hilltop temples including Jalakanteswara, Kashi Visweswara, and Gangadhareswara. Limited official information on facilities, timings, or fees.
waterDetails: Perennial spring water at Basavanna's mouth; potability not officially confirmed

name: Ramadevara Betta
shortDescription: Vulture sanctuary and Sholay filming location with hilltop temples
description: Ramadevara Betta (Ramagiri) in Ramanagara district is India's only Vulture Sanctuary (declared 2012, 346.41 hectares) and the filming location for Sholay. The hill features ancient Lord Rama and Lakshmana temples at the summit, accessed via 200–300 steps. Closes at 5:30 PM; last entry 4:00 PM. Water available near temple pond.
parkingDetails: Parking at base near the arch
waterDetails: Water available near temple pond at summit

name: Devarayanadurga
shortDescription: Hill station with ancient Narasimha temples and fort ruins
description: Devarayanadurga is a hill station in Tumakuru district, ~70 km from Bengaluru and 15 km from Tumkur. It features two ancient temples: Bhoga Narasimha (foothills, 1000+ years old) and Yoga Narasimha (hilltop). Vehicle access available to hilltop temple. Trekking trails of varying difficulty exist. Limited official information on specific timings, fees, or permits.
